refused_no_pack_point.why: The same 404 `no_pack_for_country` as `refused_no_pack`, on /v1/places/point. Added 28 Oct 2026 for a host whose proxy allowlists paths and does not admit /v1/places/generation: their own layer answered that example before it left them, so their check on `error.code` passed without ever reaching us. Same coordinate as the `point` example, so the only difference between the two is the country and therefore the refusal. Needs a host key: requireHost runs before the country check, so a keyless call here is 401 and never refuses on the pack.

locality_search_za.why: A locality hit from PRODUCTION, reproducible with your own host key. Covers `codes.same_name_as_parent`, which 2,134 of South Africa's 9,215 localities carry and a host's gate reads; `codes.osm_type`/`codes.osm_id`, which are a locality's identity rather than its name; and `lng`/`lat` with `bbox` ABSENT, which is what a point-shaped cell returns -- a transport that substitutes a zero-extent box for the missing bbox would pass every other example here. Aeroton is a locality whose name matches its sub-place parent's, which is why it carries the mark.

locality_search_in.why: The same shape from a pack whose official tiers differ: India fills one place level below ADM3, so this locality's parent chain is shorter than the South African one above. From the dev deployment, because India is not in production -- so a host that cannot reach that deployment should skip it and read `locality_search_za` instead. It stays after South Africa made it non-essential, for two reasons: the second-deployment mechanism has to keep running to keep working, and the mark is the COMMON case there and the uncommon case here -- 18,672 of the 34,424 localities in the India pack this generator reads carry it, against 2,134 of South Africa's 9,215 -- so a host sizing a gate on it from South Africa alone would be measuring the rarer half.

crosswalk.why: What became of a cell, with `basis` on every successor. New in 0.28.0.

_generated_elsewhere_why: These examples come from a non-production deployment, because the field they exercise exists only where a pack exists and that pack is not in production. Both deployments serve contract 0.30.1, asserted at generation time. The response shape is the shape production returns for the same path; the DATA in these examples is not fetchable from https://places.fascia.network, so assert their key paths and not their values. Every example carries `generated_from_public`: branch on that boolean rather than on the URL, which for a non-public deployment is a loopback address that means nothing from where you are reading it. Do not send these paths through your transport and expect a match.
_not_covered_note: Fields no example here exercises are not protected by this file. An optional field only appears when the data warrants it, so coverage is a property of the calls above. And coverage is a property of the calls you actually RUN: every example carries `key_paths_unique_to_this_example`, the key paths produced by that example and no other. If your gate skips an example -- because your own layer will not forward its path, or because `generated_from_public` is false and you have no route to the deployment it came from -- those paths stop being tested at that moment. Print them beside the reason for the skip. An empty list means the skip costs nothing.

_not_covered_why.effective_from: No layer in this deployment carries one. `effective_from` appears on a layer that is published and not yet in force, and none is today -- so no call against this pack can produce it. It is listed rather than quietly omitted: a host asserting against this file is not protected on that field.
_not_covered_why.rejected: New in 0.30.0, and not reachable from any public deployment -- a named gap, not an oversight. `rejected` is written only by the LOCALITY crosswalk, and a locality crosswalk needs TWO locality vintages of one country. No locality layer is in production at all today, and the first country to get one will still have a single vintage until its next extract. The `crosswalk` example above is sub-place ground computed from polygon overlap, which refuses nothing and so carries no `rejected`. Earliest it can be covered: one extract after a locality layer goes public. Until then, assert nothing on `rejected` through this file and treat your transport as unverified for it.
_not_covered_why.reason: `rejected[].reason` cannot be covered while `rejected` is not -- same cause, listed separately because a host searching this list for one field should not have to know it is a child of the other.
